target.title: Apply consented grouped Claw updates
target.body:
## Summary  - Extends experimental `claws update` from the read-only plan in #102959 to consented mutation across agent config, managed workspace files, packages, MCP declarations, cron jobs, and root provenance. - Requires both `--yes` and the exact `--plan-integrity` printed by the latest dry run. Immediately before mutation, it rebuilds the plan and rejects changed targets, live state, or ownership boundaries. - Applies each owner through compare-and-swap checks and compensates completed reversible owners in reverse order if a later owner fails. - Advances root package/version/integrity provenance only after every owner succeeds. - Reports `update_partial` when a package installer, source-config writer, or Gateway scheduler mutation cannot be proven fully compensated.  This remains behind `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1` and is the mutation stage for the preceding read-only update plan.  Stack references: - RFC: openclaw/rfcs#27 - Base/read-only planner: #102959 - Control UI plugin lifecycle alignment: #103176  ## Lifecycle contract  ```bash openclaw claws update <claw-or-agent> --from <source> --dry-run --json openclaw claws update <claw-or-agent> --from <source> \   --yes --plan-integrity <sha256-from-dry-run> --json ```  The executor binds consent to the full plan and fails closed if the target or current ownership changes before an individual mutation.  - **Workspace:** rooted filesystem operations verify expected source digest, destination presence/content, and provenance before each write. - **Packages:** exact ClawHub versions use shared installers and lifecycle leases. Referenced removals release only this Claw's row; managed removals use the existing package-removal planner and uninstall path before releasing provenance. Package installer outcomes without a mutation receipt remain explicitly uncertain. - **MCP:** validated config writes use compare-and-swap expectations. Removal distinguishes deleting an exact managed declaration from releasing referenced ownership. - **Cron:** Gateway-owned operations converge on stable Claw declaration keys and preserve explicit partial-state semantics for non-transactional scheduler writes. - **Provenance:** package, MCP, workspace, cron, and root writes preserve the final managed/referenced, origin, and independent-owner model from the preceding lifecycle PRs.  ## Real behavior proof  An earlier isolated WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 stack head exercised grouped preview, consented apply, and status for agent config, managed workspace files, and a remote OAuth MCP declaration. That transcript is prior-head evidence, not exact-head proof for this restack.  Live exact package replacement, Gateway-backed cron convergence, and retained-artifact diagnosis/recovery remain explicit maintainer proof requests before merge. The current head has focused injected and SQLite coverage for those mutation, race, rollback, and partial-state contracts. The initial experimental recovery contract is fail closed, report `update_partial`, preserve uncertain state, and require operator inspection/replanning; a richer doctor/reconcile operation identity remains a maintainer follow-up choice.  ## Validation  Current head: `3667eb6d4e07d922742aca9d4a601d6c62c52e0f`.  - 82 focused unit and CLI tests pass across update execution, package lifecycle/provenance, workspace, MCP, cron, root provenance, and CLI consent. - Real SQLite regressions cover package reference CAS, managed uninstall/release distinctions, MCP release rollback, and complete ownership timestamps. - Race regressions cover disappearing agents/workspace targets, source MCP changes, concurrent package ownership, stale release provenance, and plugin preflight rejection. - Changed-file `oxfmt`, `oxlint --deny-warnings`, and `git diff --check` pass. - Exact branch review against `82bcde001d69249e9b880301ae6974d6e5296196`: `autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported` after fixing consent, package digest/release/remove, and stale-agent races.
- Exact-SHA GitHub CI passed at [run 29676105624](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29676105624), including production/test types, lint, dependency guards, Node core tests, and macOS Swift. - Full local production typecheck is not claimed: the reused WSL dependency tree has unrelated `semver`, `p-limit`, and `execa` skew. GitHub CI is the authoritative full type/dependency proof for this head.  ## Stack note  This is a ready stacked PR. Do not merge it before #102959 and the earlier Claws ownership/lifecycle slices settle.

target.title: fix(agents): stop runs at the critical tool-loop threshold
target.body:
Closes #106231

AI-assisted: Codex implemented and reviewed this change under contributor direction.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an agent that reached the critical tool-loop threshold would only emit a warning and continue running. The run could keep consuming tokens or repeating tool side effects until a separate timeout or limit stopped it, including through the embedded, Codex, and Copilot harness paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

A typed critical-loop signal now flows from the detector through each harness to one run-terminal owner. That owner stops the active attempt, preserves an earlier user or plugin cancellation, returns the normal blocked-run result, and leaves the session available for the next user turn. Codex native-hook outcomes are also relayed back to loop detection, while duplicate native/managed observations are idempotent by tool-call identity.

## User Impact

Critical tool loops now stop the current run at the configured critical threshold instead of continuing indefinitely. Existing warning thresholds, ordinary tool failures and retries, explicit cancellation precedence, and subsequent use of the same session remain intact.

## Compatibility

This adds no new configuration or storage surface.

The existing Codex `loopDetectionPreToolUseRelay` switch currently governs the paired loop-detection relay path: setting it to `false` disables both the loop-only `PreToolUse` marker and its companion `PostToolUse` outcome relay. The outcome relay only completes loop history created by the matching pre-tool observation, so retaining it alone would not provide an independent detection capability. No separate PostToolUse-only setting is introduced.

This does not disable relays required by plugin hooks, trusted-tool policy, or result middleware. The reference and troubleshooting documentation state the paired opt-out explicitly.

**Maintainer decision requested:** Please confirm whether the existing `false` value must preserve its historical PreToolUse-only opt-out, or whether it is now the supported opt-out for the paired PreToolUse/PostToolUse loop-detection path. The current implementation uses the paired behavior. If the historical narrow contract must be preserved, I will adjust the implementation and focused configuration tests before merge. After that decision, I will refresh the final branch against current `main` and rerun exact-head CI.

## Evidence

### Redacted runtime proof

Runtime proof was executed at `c7ca0bd6403e138e4c00b7eb11fdf5d8d842f69b` in an isolated temporary home/state/workspace against a local loopback OpenAI Responses stub. It used no AWS service, external model, external credential, or user data. Current exact head `19d9e8da730a29375d4b091f9652b104feb27c1e` is a patch-preserving rebase onto `3fd3ad83014897ead39d394d8d72b25bfe2f3f83`: both commit patch IDs are unchanged, upstream touched none of this PR's files at the rebase point, and `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passes.

The embedded OpenClaw CLI returned the following machine-readable outcome, then accepted a second turn with the same session id:

```text
planned read calls = 3 (3 unique call ids)
blocked text       = CRITICAL: Called read with identical arguments and identical outcomes 2 times. Session execution blocked to prevent runaway loops.
livenessState      = blocked
error.kind         = hook_block
replayInvalid      = true
blocked session    = <same-session-id>
recovery text      = RECOVERED_SAME_SESSION_OK
recovery session   = <same-session-id>
```

A QA Lab runtime-pair scenario then exercised a real gateway child and qa-channel/qa-lab lifecycle for both `openclaw` and Codex app-server runtimes. Both cells passed. Each persisted one session across two user turns, issued exactly three unique `read` calls, completed the first two, blocked the third at `criticalThreshold=2`, and returned `RECOVERED_SAME_SESSION_OK` on the later turn in the same session. Codex recorded the third tool result as `isError=true` with `OpenClaw dynamic tool call aborted.`

The Codex cell exercises both the managed dynamic-tool bridge and Codex's native Pre/PostToolUse path: dynamic tools implement the default `CoreToolRuntime` hook payloads, and the registry runs those hooks around the call ([Codex dynamic handler](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/2895d82b5e449407712439ba4f89954f3fa0c7e3/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/dynamic.rs), [Codex registry](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/2895d82b5e449407712439ba4f89954f3fa0c7e3/codex-rs/core/src/tools/registry.rs#L490-L603)). Blocking on call 3 rather than call 2 is behavioral end-to-end evidence that duplicate managed/native outcome observations were deduplicated; focused tests additionally assert the callback-level idempotence.

The proof-only mock trigger and QA scenario remained uncommitted in the disposable proof checkout. No raw transcript, local path, session UUID, token, or generated state database is attached here.

### Deterministic and review proof

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.critical-tool-loop.test.ts`: 7/7 passed. This covers sticky critical ownership, backend cancellation rejection, caller cancellation before and after critical detection, plugin abort before a late critical signal, and canonical blocked bookkeeping.
- Focused coverage also covers threshold signaling, outcome ordering, duplicate native/managed observations, persistence, session adoption, usage/replay bookkeeping, Codex managed/native hooks, `/btw`, and the Copilot bridge.
- Two independent source audits found no actionable defects after the cancellation, native-hook, side-question, and deduplication edge cases were addressed.
- Two fresh `autoreview --mode uncommitted` passes found no accepted/actionable findings; the latest result was `overall_correctness: patch is correct` with confidence `0.97`.
- Exact-head GitHub Actions passed the authoritative `openclaw/ci-gate`, build, production types, lint, docs, security, all four QA Smoke profiles, and every changed-surface test. No current required check is failing.

### Dependency contract

Checked directly against `openai/codex@2895d82b5e449407712439ba4f89954f3fa0c7e3`: [`success: false` dynamic-tool responses remain normal tool outputs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/2895d82b5e449407712439ba4f89954f3fa0c7e3/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/dynamic.rs), and native pre/post hooks share the tool call identity and response lifecycle ([registry dispatch](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/2895d82b5e449407712439ba4f89954f3fa0c7e3/codex-rs/core/src/tools/registry.rs#L490-L603)).
